description: The LoS debug overlay must answer the SAME question as the target list. It used to answer 'is there a clear sight line', so a squad the game refuses to shoot was painted solid green (reported 2026-08: Custodian Guard -> Stormboyz, 'there is at least one green line between the two squads but the target is not an option') and a squad that WAS a legal target could be painted red, because the overlay ran its own 1-3 pair loop with an extra TerrainManager.model_visible_11e gate the rules path never applies. Board: a Custodian Guard (24" Guardian spear) with Boyz Gamma 15" away up a clear corridor (LEGAL TARGET) and Kommandos 32" away up the same corridor (clear sight line, OUT OF RANGE). Green must mean targetable and nothing else; the out-of-range squad must come back amber with the reason written on the line; and with a shooter armed the overlay must volunteer that reason instead of drawing nothing at all for the squad the player cannot select. Also drives Settings > Visual > "LoS Debug: include units out of weapon range" through the real menu: with it off, the out-of-range squad is dropped before any line-of-sight work happens, so the overlay only talks about enemies your guns can actually reach.

steps.comment: The hot-seat handoff screen is a full-screen CanvasLayer that eats input; acknowledge it the way the player's [Enter] does before driving anything.
Setup: one Custodian Guard and two Ork squads in a clear vertical corridor at board x=12"; everything else removed from play so the overlay draws exactly the two lines under test.
Ground truth from the rules engine: Boyz Gamma IS in the target list, Kommandos is NOT. Every assertion below is about the overlay agreeing with this.
…and the refusal is a RANGE refusal, not a sight-line one — which is exactly why a pure-LoS overlay drew it green.
The unit-level sight line is CLEAR for both squads: the two units really can see each other. Pinning this is what makes the green/amber split meaningful rather than an accident of geometry.
Guard the hard-coded row index below against fixture drift.
Shooter mode: the per-model fan still covers the eligible target…
…and the squad the player CANNOT select now gets a summary line carrying the reason. Before the fix this list was empty and the overlay said nothing whatsoever about Kommandos.
Now the unit->unit overview — the exact call Main._toggle_los_debug() makes when L is held with no shooter armed. Both squads get a line and the verdicts must split.
The out-of-range squad's line carries the player-facing reason, drawn on the line itself.

THE invariant, checked over every line the overlay drew: a solid-green line means the target list will accept that unit, and every unit the target list accepts is drawn green. Deliberately falls back to the pre-fix line shape (is_clear, no verdict key) so this fails on BEHAVIOUR rather than on a missing API when run against the old overlay — where it reports 2 mismatches: the legal target painted red and the out-of-range squad painted green.
Precondition: the setting ships ON, but it is persisted in user://settings.cfg, so a machine that ran this suite before could start from OFF.
Main._open_settings_menu is the shared entry point the Escape handler and windowed scenarios both use.
Real clicks from here on — the settings menu is built procedurally, so there is no stable NodePath to aim at and button_text is the resolver scenarios use for it.
The checkbox reflects the shipped default before we touch it.

steps.button_text: LoS Debug: include units out of weapon range

steps.comment: The checkbox actually wrote through to the service (and thus to settings.cfg).
With the setting off the out-of-range squad is gone entirely — not amber, not red, absent — while the squad you CAN shoot is untouched.
…and turning it back on through the same menu path restores the amber line, so the toggle is genuinely two-way.

steps.button_text: LoS Debug: include units out of weapon range

steps.comment: No SCRIPT ERRORs fired while driving any of the above.
